sections.h2: Where is Keizer, Oregon, and what is it next to?
sections.html:
Keizer is a city in Marion County, in the Willamette Valley about 3 miles north of downtown Salem and 43 miles south of Portland. It is part of the Salem metropolitan area, and Salem borders it on the south and east.

The Willamette River forms the southwestern edge of the city and separates it from Polk County. The city measures about 4,713 acres, or 7.36 square miles, and Keizer's ZIP codes are 97303 and 97307.

sections.h2: How did Keizer get its name and become a city?
sections.html:
Keizer takes its name from Thomas Dove Keizur, a pioneer who came west with the Wagon Train of 1843, and a clerk misspelled his name in land claim records.

The first settlement sat near the river at Keizer Bottom. A flood in 1861 damaged it, and residents moved to higher ground. Salem tried more than once to annex the community, and neighbors began organizing a separate city in 1964. Voters finally incorporated Keizer on November 2, 1982, on the seventh attempt, by a vote of 4,440 to 3,341. About 19,650 people lived here at that point.

The 1990s then brought rapid residential growth, so a good share of the city's houses are now about three decades old, and some are older still.

sections.h2: How many people live in Keizer?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 39,140 residents in Keizer as of July 1, 2025, and the 2020 census counted 39,376.

Keizer is the 14th most populous city in Oregon. The count rose 7.9 percent from 2010 to 2020, and about 22 percent of residents identify as Hispanic or Latino.

sections.h2: Does Keizer flood, and does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, parts of Keizer sit in the Willamette River floodplain, and flood history is a normal topic when a house is on the market.

Floods in 1861, 1943, 1945, 1946 and 1948 slowed growth, and dams built on the river in the 1950s helped regulate it. The February 1996 flood damaged several homes, and some residents received FEMA funds to move out of the floodplain. A 2024 local news report cited First Street Foundation estimates that about 3,060 Keizer properties, 53 percent of the city, carry a greater than 26 percent chance of severe flood impact over 30 years. That is a modeled risk figure from a private group, so treat it as context and check the official maps for any specific address.

Areas named in the same report as sensitive to high water include Claggett Creek, Chemawa Road NE, Keizer Rapids Park and Spong's Landing. The city has a floodplain overlay zone in its code, and Marion County runs a floodplain program. Before you list, find out whether your lot is mapped and whether you carry flood insurance. A buyer's lender will ask, and answers you can document keep the deal moving.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Keizer?
sections.html:
Keizer shares the Salem-area climate: warm dry summers and a wet cool season from October through April.

Salem's mean July high is about 83.5 degrees, annual precipitation is about 40 inches, and snow averages roughly 3.5 inches a year. The all-time record high at Salem is 117 degrees, set in June, and the record low is minus 12 degrees, set in December. That adds up to months of steady rain on roofs, gutters and crawl spaces every year, and sellers who skipped upkeep tend to hear about it in inspections.

sections.h2: Who employs people in and around Keizer?
sections.html:
Most Keizer residents work elsewhere, and the largest nearby employers are in Salem.

Keizer's own draft strategic plan says the city relies on surrounding cities for employment and wants more retail, medical clinics and light industry. One local retail area is Keizer Station, where a 14-acre site called Chemawa Station at Ulali Drive and Chemawa Road is owned by the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde and the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians.

sections.h2: What roads and schools serve Keizer?
sections.html:
Interstate 5 runs along the northeast border of Keizer, with access at Exit 260A on Chemawa Road NE, and Oregon Route 99E runs just outside the southeastern limit.

River Road congestion is expected to worsen, and the city is improving Verda Lane between Salem Parkway and Chemawa Road as a possible north-south alternative. Some residents of the older neighborhood between Chemawa Road and Lockhaven Drive have raised concerns about extending it north.

Keizer belongs to the Salem-Keizer School District, formed in 1955 when Keizer's district merged with Salem's. The city has one high school, McNary, plus Claggett Creek and Whiteaker middle schools and seven elementary schools: Clear Lake, Cummings, Forest Ridge, Gubser, Keizer, Kennedy and Weddle. The 1916 school building now holds the Keizer Heritage Community Center and Museum.

sections.h2: What is there to do in Keizer, and does it matter for a sale?
sections.html:
Keizer calls itself the Iris Capital of the World, and its parks and festivals are part of the pitch to buyers.

KeizerFEST, the Iris Festival, takes place each May. Schreiner's Iris Gardens, one of the largest retail iris growers in the country, founded it, and the Keizer Chamber of Commerce has helped run it since 1987. The city maintains 18 parks covering more than 200 acres. Keizer Rapids Park has river frontage, trails, a dog park and an amphitheater, and Keizer Stadium, which opened in 1997, hosts the Salem-Keizer Volcanoes. Fifteen underground wells supply the city's water.

Mention nearby parks, the festival and the school buildings in your listing or when you speak with a cash buyer, since they describe the neighborhood in ways a photo cannot.

sections.h2: What are the property tax dates in Marion County?
sections.html:
Marion County mails property tax statements between October 15 and 25, and the first payment is due November 15. Pay in full by that date for a 3 percent discount, or pay two-thirds for a 2 percent discount with the last third due May 15.

The one-third option has no discount, with the remaining installments due February 15 and May 15. Payments sent by mail must be postmarked by November 15. If your statement has not arrived by November 1, the Tax Department asks you to call (503) 588-5215. The county applies payments to the oldest tax year with a balance first, which matters if a past year is unpaid on a house you plan to sell.

Details are on the Marion County payment information page. Your title company will prorate the current year at closing.

sections.h2: What do Keizer sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers in Keizer tend to meet a few repeat issues, and a cash sale can address several of them.

  • Flood questions: buyers and lenders ask about mapping and insurance.
  • Aging houses: homes from the 1990s growth period can need new roofs, windows and systems.
  • Limited land: the city's plan says it lacks enough land for needed housing, and an urban growth boundary limits expansion.
  • Small-lot infill: developers are using state law to build clusters of up to four homes on lots once zoned for one.

If you want to avoid repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal, ask a cash buyer for terms in writing and compare them with a listing. Closing is handled by a title company in either case.
